record_under_review.evidence_span: Tasa addresses the thermal limits of 3D-stacked architectures by combining heterogeneous high-performance and high-efficiency cores with cross-stack thermal optimization and bandwidth-sharing scheduling. The abstract reports peak-temperature reductions of 5.55, 9.37, and 7.91 degrees Celsius for 48, 60, and 72 core configurations, plus 2.85x and 2.21x speedups for Llama-65B and GPT-3 66B inference over GPU baselines and a heterogeneous PIM accelerator.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: 3D-stacked multi-DRAM-die-over-logic architecture with thermal constraints and heterogeneous cores; technology, cooling, and memory-stack assumptions require full-paper verification.
record_under_review.limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; full-paper verification is needed for thermal-model calibration, area/cost overhead, memory bandwidth assumptions, and comparison fairness.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: Heterogeneous 3D-stacked architecture with high-performance cores for compute-intensive operators, high-efficiency cores for memory-intensive attention operators, cross-stack thermal balancing, and bandwidth-sharing scheduling.
record_under_review.problem: 3D stacking increases memory bandwidth for autoregressive LLM decoding but creates more severe temperature, thermal-gradient, and scalability constraints than 2D designs.
record_under_review.title: Tasa: Thermal-aware 3D-Stacked Architecture Design with Bandwidth Sharing for LLM Inference
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: Llama-65B and GPT-3 66B inference with 48-, 60-, and 72-core configurations; comparisons include GPU and heterogeneous PIM-based accelerators.
